skinInspector.soundEnemyAnyInfo: Every kill of an enemy without sounds of its own
skinInspector.soundEnemyInfo: With an enemy picked, kills of that enemy play this group instead; kills of an enemy without its own sounds play the Any enemy group. The list is read from the game's own enemy data; type a name to search.
skinInspector.soundEnemyUnknown: An enemy this game does not have (id {{v0}})
skinInspector.soundWeightInfo: A group (one event; for kills, one enemy) plays one sound each time: picked at random by weight, chance = its weight / the group's total, and never the same sound twice in a row.
skinInspector.soundLowAmmoInfo: Low-ammo sounds share this threshold: the group plays once when the clip falls below it.
skinInspector.attachInfo: An ammo screen shows ammo or kills live; a model can be any .glb or .gltf file. New ones mount on the selected part; you can move them to another part later.
skinInspector.noAttachments: Nothing mounted on this part yet.

exportMod.noIcon: No icon yet; choose an image

actions.building: The last build has not finished yet; try again when it is done.
errors.nothingToApply: Nothing in this skin can go into the game files: only textures and material settings (metallic, smoothness, glow, colour) can.
errors.gameChanged: The game files changed meanwhile (a game update or a Steam file check). Open “Restore original game assets” to see the state, then try again.
errors.stalePatch: The game files still hold skins written for an older game version. Run “Verify integrity of game files” in Steam, then try again.
errors.badBackup: The backup of an original file is missing or damaged, so it can’t be restored. Run “Verify integrity of game files” in Steam; it puts the originals back.
gameFiles.groupInfo: No plugin needed: textures and material settings are written straight into the game’s own asset files, after backing up the originals. Attachments, screens, animated textures, sounds and layout changes can’t go in. A game update or a Steam file check puts the originals back.
gameFiles.replaceWhat: Writes the textures and material settings of “{{v0}}” straight into GTFO’s game files (the originals are backed up and can be restored at any time). No plugin needed; other players still see their own files.
gameFiles.notWritten: These can’t go into the game files and are skipped:
gameFiles.closeGame: Close the game first: it holds these files while it runs.
gameFiles.applied: Written to the game files; shows the next time the game starts
gameFiles.applyFailed: Could not write the game files
gameFiles.none: No skins are written into the game files right now.
gameFiles.restoreFailed: Could not restore the game files
gameFiles.stale: There are records from an older game version. After a game update those backups can’t be used; verify the game files in Steam, then clear these records.
gameFiles.exportFailed: Could not export the game asset pack
gameFiles.w.shared: “{{v0}}” is a shared material, so these change too: {{v1}}
gameFiles.w.unused: “{{v0}}” isn’t used by this item; skipped

gameFiles.w.alpha: “{{v0}}” has no transparency in the game; the image’s transparent parts are dropped

skinInspector.texSizeMemory: About {{v0}} of video memory in game

Larger makes text and lines in the paint sharper, and takes more video memory and a larger skin file. Auto: at least 2048 for a painted part, the image's own size otherwise.
welcome.exampleDone: The example skin is ready: a painted {{v0}}, an ammo screen and a hologram ring. Open them on the left to see how each is set up.

addMenu.title: Add to this part
leftRail.pendingInfo: Some textures were matched with low confidence. Click to confirm them.
partModel.title: Model
partModel.info: Replace this node’s model with your own .glb or .gltf. Only its own model changes: child parts stay, textures and materials still apply, and position, rotation and scale stay editable.
topBar.testProfileInfo: Apply installs only into this profile, for your own testing; a running game shows it in seconds. To give the skin to others, use Export.
topBar.autoApplyInfo: On: the work in use is applied to the game 2 seconds after each change (only while the game runs). Off: its card says “Changes not applied”; click Apply to update.
actions.pluginMissing: “{{v0}}” has no skin plugin yet. Installing the editor's {{v1}} first, then the skin.
actions.pluginWrong: The skin plugin in “{{v0}}” is {{v1}}; the editor ships {{v2}}. Replacing it with the editor's first, then the skin.
livery.title: Livery
livery.info: Like a racing game's livery editor: pick a finish, then stack base coats, decals and brush strokes. Layers higher in the list sit on top. Packing bakes everything into the part's textures, so the game sees ordinary textures, and “Replace game files” works too.
livery.finishInfo: Sets how metallic and glossy the part looks. It makes the part's metallic/smoothness texture; Glow makes the paint itself light up.
livery.empty: No paint layers yet. Add one with the buttons above.
livery.blendInfo: Normal covers what is below. Multiply only darkens and keeps the detail below (use it for a base coat that keeps the original texture). Screen only lightens. Overlay boosts contrast. Add brightens like light.
livery.depthInfo: How far the decal prints into and out from the surface. Too much prints on the far side of the part; too little cuts it off on curves.
livery.placeHint: In the 3D view, press on this part and drag: it slides along the surface and turns with its curves.
livery.notPlaced: Not placed yet: click this part in the 3D view.
livery.brushHint: Drag on the part in the 3D view to paint; pick the shape and width in the bar over the view.
livery.maskInfo: Wherever the mask is painted, this layer is hidden. Turn on “Paint mask” and drag in the 3D view.
livery.bar.decal: Drag on the part: move the decal
livery.bar.mask: Drag on the part: paint the mask
livery.bar.fill: Turn on Paint mask to keep areas free of this coat
livery.playbackHint: {{v0}} frames. In game the decal plays like a dynamic layer; until it plays it shows its first frame. Paint above and below it is baked into every frame.
livery.badImage: This image cannot be opened. Try a PNG or JPG.
errors.noLiveryView: The livery is baked in the 3D view: wait until the weapon shows there, then try again.
errors.duplicateMaterial: Two overrides edit the same material: keep one of them and try again.
errors.badMaterialTarget: A decal or animated layer sits on an attachment that has no model: delete it, or put it on an attachment with a model, and try again.
errors.workInUse: Another program has this work's files open (an image editor, a folder window, or a virus scan). Close it or wait a few seconds and delete again; nothing was deleted.
errors.restartEditor: The editor needs a restart for this: close it and open it again.
errors.fileInUse: Another program has the file open: close it and try again.
errors.settingsUnreadable: The editor's settings file (settings.json in its data folder) could not be read: another program has it open or it is damaged. It was left unchanged. Close that program and try again; if the file is damaged, fix it or move it away and restart the editor (then add your own profiles again).
errors.damagedGameFile: A game file could not be read; most likely another way of skinning edited it directly. In your Steam library, right-click GTFO → Properties → Installed Files → Verify integrity of game files, then try again.
shapes.title: Shapes
hologram.title: Hologram
hologram.info: Drawn in game as a glowing, flickering hologram with the game's own hologram shader, in the model's colour and the screen's colours.
topBar.update.dev: A development run does not update; the installed app checks
topBar.update.downloading: A new version is downloading in the background; you will be asked to restart when it is ready
topBar.update.error: Could not check for updates; check the network and try again
topBar.update.portable: The portable copy does not update itself; download the new version from the releases page and unzip it over this folder. Your data folder is not touched
dataDir.title: Data folder
dataDir.info.installed: Autosaved skins, caches, built packs and logs live here. By default it is Documents\ForgeSkin. Changing it moves all of your data over and deletes the old folder only once the copy is checked.
dataDir.info.portable: Autosaved skins, caches, built packs and logs live here. The portable copy keeps them in GTFO_UserData next to the program by default. Changing it moves all of your data over and deletes the old folder only once the copy is checked.
dataDir.info.dev: A development run always uses GTFO_UserData in the checkout.
dataDir.adopted: Now using the ForgeSkin data already in {{v0}}; the old folder was left as it was
dataDir.leftover: Data moved, but the old folder could not be fully deleted; you can delete it yourself: {{v0}}
dataDir.same: This is already the data folder
dataDir.nested: The new place cannot be inside the current data folder or contain it; pick another folder
dataDir.notEmpty: This folder already holds other files that are not ForgeSkin data. Pick an empty folder (you can make one in the dialog)
dataDir.failed: The move did not finish; your data is still in its old place and nothing was lost: {{v0}}
dataDir.dev: A development run cannot change its data folder
exportMod.formatForge: ForgeSkin format: every effect (dynamic layers, attachments, sounds, part changes), applied by the ForgeSkin plugin.
exportMod.formatSkins: Skins format: for players with the Skins library (food-Skins). Each skin is its own skin group, a weapon may get several, and players pick in game. Still textures and material settings only; dynamic layers, attachments, sounds, part changes, wear stages and item skins are left out.
exportMod.doneDropped: Thunderstore skin mod exported; {{v0}} things were left out or changed, the list is open
skins.notGroup: Pick the manifest.skingroup.json in the skin group folder
app.updateReady: A new version is downloaded; restart ForgeSkin to use it (the plugin updates too).
app.filesChanged: Files changed outside the editor, read again: {{v0}}
livery.wearInfo: Wears the paint below away by the model’s edges, bumps and random patches, showing the game’s own texture and metal. Edges go first.
livery.killsToFullInfo: 0 = fixed wear. Above 0 the gun starts clean and wears in four stages with your kills with it, reaching the amount above at this many kills. Kills are counted per skin and gun.
variants.title: Colour variants
variants.info: Several colourings of one skin. With one selected, livery colour edits change only it. Apply uses the selected one; an exported mod has each as its own skin (named “ · variant”).
charm.title: Charm
charm.info: Hangs this attachment on a cord, chain or beads from its point on the gun (the orange dot in the 3D view); the model hangs at the rope's end. In game it sways with gravity and swings as you run, turn, jump and shoot, only on the gun in your own hands. Run and Turn below show it here.
charm.runInfo: Runs forward for two seconds and stops
charm.menuHint: Hangs on a rope from the gun
charm.pointHint: The orange dot is where the rope is fixed to the gun. Drag the arrows in the 3D view to move it; the model hangs at the rope's end.
stickers.title: Stickers
livery.shape.fill: Fill a piece (click: the whole UV island is painted or masked)
livery.mirrorInfo: Also paints the mirror image on the gear's other side (across its centre plane); fills too
playerColors.title: Player colours
playerColors.info: Colours players can change themselves in game, in the skin picker. One player colour can drive several places (say the body tint and the screen digits); they always change together.
playerColors.empty: None yet. Click the person button next to a colour to let players change it.
playerColors.name: Name
playerColors.remove: Players can no longer change this
playerColors.toggle: Let players change this colour in game
help.title: Tutorial
tour.skipAsk: To go through it again later, click the book button in the top bar and pick a chapter under Guided tours.
tour.waiting: Waiting for this button to appear…
tour.missing: Can't find the spot to click. Click Next to skip this step.
tour.ready: This step is already done; click Next.
tour.introInfo: Click where it lights up and you will have a skin in the game in a few minutes. Each step moves on by itself once done; press Esc to leave at any time.
tour.profileInfo: Click the lit button and pick the r2modman profile you play GTFO with; the skin goes there. If it is already that one, click Next.
tour.weaponInfo: Click “+ New” to open the gear list and pick one to skin. If a work is already open, you can click Next.
tour.newSkinInfo: Click a gear in the list and you have a new work called “gear name skin”. It is your practice work: it is deleted when the guide ends or you leave it, and the gear's look in game is not touched.
tour.partInfo: Click the gun in the 3D view, the receiver for example, to select that part.
tour.textureInfo: Click Textures on the right, then the lit Albedo slot to choose an image, or drop an image on it. No image at hand? Click Use the sample texture below.
tour.previewInfo: Drag to turn the gun, scroll to zoom, and try Fire and Kill under the view. Click Next when you are done.
tour.saveInfo: Your changes are saved already; the status bar says Autosaved. To keep a file of your own, click More → Save to file… and pick a place in the window that opens. Otherwise click Next.
tour.applyInfo: Click Apply on the work's card. The editor packs it, installs it into the profile named at the top left and has your gear wear it in game. A running game changes within seconds; otherwise it shows the next time you start.
tour.finishInfo: That is the whole way a skin is made. When the guide closes, this practice work is deleted and taken out of the profile; for a real one, click a gear in the list to make a new work. Liveries, animated layers, attachments, the ammo screen and player colours are all in the written tutorial.
tour.charIntro: Wear a character of your own
tour.charIntroInfo: Turn a humanoid .vrm or .glb model into a character skin that replaces you in game. Have a model file ready, then click where it lights up.
tour.charModeInfo: Click Characters at the top of the left column; the works list then shows characters only.
tour.charNewInfo: Click + New and choose your .vrm or .glb file. Once it is in, the left column shows the six steps of a character.
tour.charBonesInfo: The editor matches the model's bones to the game's skeleton by itself. When the right side says the bones all match, you are done; click a joint with a red dot to pick another bone.
tour.charSpringsInfo: In step 4, Hair and skirt, the editor has found the hair, skirt and tails that sway. Click Jolt or Run below to watch them, and drag Stiffness if they are too soft or too stiff.
tour.charApplyInfo: Click Apply on the character's card. It goes into the profile at the top left and you wear it in game; a running game shows it from the next level.
tour.charFinishInfo: To go back to the original character, open SKINS in the game's lobby and change the CHARACTER cell at the top. Materials, first-person arms and the rest are in the written tutorial under Character models.
tour.profIntroInfo: A profile is an r2modman game profile. A work installed into a profile shows up in the game started from that profile.
tour.profPickInfo: Click the Apply to: row and pick a profile. The top of the menu shows that profile: whether the game runs and which skin plugin version it has; a missing or old plugin can be installed there. A grey profile has no BepInEx and cannot be used.
tour.profStatesInfo: The top left of each work's picture says how it stands in this profile: Only in the editor (grey), the game cannot see it; In the profile (blue), it can be picked on the game's skin page but is not worn; In use (green), the game wears it on this gear, and the card has a green frame. In each group, works in use come first. Switch profiles and these change with it.
tour.profMore: Into and out of the profile
tour.profMoreInfo: Apply on a card installs and wears it; to go back to the original look, change it in the game's skin picker. Point at a card for ⋯ at the top right of its picture, or right-click the card for the same menu: Put in profile puts it in without wearing it, Take out of profile sends the file to the recycle bin.
tour.profOthers: Other people's skins in the profile
tour.profOthersInfo: Skin packs by others in this profile are folded into one bar at the top of the list that says how many there are; open it to see their cards, which can be applied too. Move all makes them your works to edit. To install a pack someone sent you, use Add packs… under the arrow next to New.
tour.profFinishInfo: Keep a test profile for trying skins, and only finished ones in the profile you play with.
tour.hotIntro: Change it while the game runs
tour.hotIntroInfo: The skin plugin watches the profile's skins folder. Once the editor installs a skin, a running game wears it within seconds, with no restart and no trip to the in-game skin page.
tour.hotStatusInfo: The bottom left says how things stand: with the game running, an apply shows within seconds; with the game closed, it shows the next time you start.
tour.hotApplyInfo: When you have made a change, click Apply on the card. A work in use that you changed says Changes not applied on its card; Apply again sends the change to the game.
tour.hotAutoInfo: Click the gear at the top right and turn on Apply automatically: two seconds after you stop changing the work in use it is applied, only while the game runs. It is off by default.
tour.hotFinishInfo: With the game running and the gear in hand, change a colour in the editor and apply: it changes in game a few seconds later. A character changes from the next level.
tour.schemeIntro: Several colour sets for one gun
tour.schemeIntroInfo: A colour scheme is a set of colours for the whole gun. Make a few, and players switch between them with a click on the game's colour page.
tour.schemeWholeInfo: Click Whole gun at the top of the parts list; the right side then shows the whole gun's settings.
tour.schemePlayerInfo: A scheme sets the player colours. Click the person button next to a colour on a livery or layer, and that colour shows up here.
tour.schemeCardsInfo: Set the colours and click + Save as scheme. Click a card and the whole gun takes that set; rename it on the card and delete it with the cross. Original is the colours you set first.
tour.schemeFinishInfo: After you apply, open this gear's colour page in game to see the schemes.
exportMod.formatPack: Skins gun pack: the whole mod is one skin group and you pick one skin per weapon below; a player who picks the pack on a weapon gets the skin you chose for it. What is left out is the same as for a group per skin.
exportMod.skinsHint: Every item with skins in the editor is listed; tick skins of any item, several for one weapon if you like.
exportMod.packHint: Weapons set to "Not in the pack" stay out.
exportMod.modelTimeout: The weapon model took too long to load, so its livery could not be baked
skinsImport.failed: Could not import the Skins skin group
skinsImport.nothing: This skin group has nothing to import
skinsImport.title: Skins skin group imported
skinsReport.list: {{v0}} things left out or changed (open to see)
skinsReport.summary: Skins and ForgeSkin do not do quite the same things; these did not come across as they were.
skinsReport.imported: Each of these items got a skin; click a name to open it:
skinsReport.targetTitle: This skin group names no weapon
skinsReport.targetBody: In Skins a skin group without a weapon id condition goes on no weapon (one with only a rundown condition neither). Pick a weapon to import it as a skin of that weapon, or cancel.
skinsNote.desc: The description of "{{skin}}" is not kept: ForgeSkin skins have none
skinsNote.meshTarget: Mesh replacement {{what}} not imported (mesh replacements are not converted)
skinsNote.noGear: Material settings {{what}} fit none of the group's weapons; not imported
skinsNote.conflict: {{what}}: the material already has settings; Skins uses only the first, so this one never showed
skinsNote.shader: Shader swap ({{what}}) not kept; the game's own shader stays
skinsNote.emptyGear: {{what}} has no material settings that fit it; no skin made for it
skinsNote.rundown: Rundown condition ({{what}}) not kept; the skin works in every rundown
skinsNote.filterType: Unknown filter type {{what}}; that condition is skipped
skinsNote.contradiction: A filter group asks for several different weapons at once ({{what}}), so Skins never uses it; skipped
skinsNote.unknownGear: The game has no gear with id {{what}}; skipped
skinsNote.textureOptions: Texture options (linear, mipmaps) of {{what}} not kept; ForgeSkin sets them per texture channel
skinsNote.property: {{what}}: ForgeSkin has no such setting; not kept
skinsNote.itemSkin: "{{skin}}" is an item skin; Skins skins only weapons and tools, so it is not in the mod
skinsNote.unusedMaterials: No weapon uses the materials of "{{skin}}"; not in the mod
skinsNote.global: "{{skin}}" is a skin for every gear with its materials: in Skins it is written for the {{n}} weapons that use them, players pick it on each weapon, and it replaces that weapon's other skin
skinsNote.sameMaterial: "{{skin}}" sets material {{what}} {{n}} more times; ForgeSkin and Skins both use only the last, the others are not written
skinsNote.sharedMaterial: {{what}} of "{{skin}}" cannot be told apart from the same material on these weapons in the pack; they get it too
skinsNote.layers: {{n}} dynamic layers on {{what}} of "{{skin}}" not kept (Skins textures are still)
skinsNote.wear: {{n}} wear stages of {{what}} in "{{skin}}" not kept; the unworn look is used
skinsNote.playerColors: {{n}} player colours of "{{skin}}" not kept; their defaults are used
skinsNote.variants: {{n}} colour variants of "{{skin}}" not in the gun pack (one skin per weapon: the base colours)
codeFx.title: Code effect
codeFx.name: Name
codeFx.whereInfo: On a part it is painted onto the part's own texture, over its pictures and animated layers. On an attached model it is drawn over the model.
codeFx.attachmentHidden: The attached model “{{v0}}” is hidden, so this effect does not show in the game.
codeFx.programInfo: Patterns are drawn live by the game, so they move and players can change them. The 3D view uses the same pattern code as the game.
codeFx.tryEvent: Play the event in the 3D view
codeFx.playerTip: Players can change this in game, on the ADJUST page of the skin picker. Their setting stays on their computer.
livery.copyToInfo: Puts a copy of this layer on each ticked part. Decals, panel lines and text need one click on their new part to be placed.
livery.copyToBrush: Brush strokes belong to this part's own texture and cannot move to another part.
livery.trimInfo: Sci-fi panel lines, cut-corner frames, double frames, ticks, corner brackets, chevrons, hazard stripes and seams, drawn in code so they stay sharp at any size. Turn on Glow for glowing seams.
livery.tileInfo: A picture repeated over the part at the size you set, projected from three sides so it runs across texture seams. Pick it from your own library or any file.
livery.placementInfo: The same values dragging in the 3D view sets: position and rotation on its part, in millimetres and degrees.
livery.symmetricInfo: Also places it at the mirror position on the gun's other side (across its centre plane). Text reads the right way round there too.
livery.glowLayerInfo: Also draws this layer into the emissive texture, so it lights up in game. The glow strength below is shared by the glowing layers of this part.
livery.fadeInfo: Fades this layer out along a direction or outwards from a centre.
library.remove: Take out of the library (skins using it keep it)
library.noStickers: No stickers of your own yet. Imported pictures are copied into the data folder for every skin.
library.noTiles: No tile images yet. Imported pictures are copied into the data folder for every skin.
palette.title: Palettes
palette.info: Save the colours this skin's livery layers use as a palette and apply it to another skin in one click. Click one to offer its colours under every colour picker. Palettes are yours and do not go into packs.
palette.name: Palette name
palette.saveInfo: Saves the first {{v0}} colours of the paint layers
palette.nothingToSave: This skin has no paint colours yet
hologram.rampInfo: Fades from the model's colour at the bottom to a second colour at the top. Built-in shapes fade bottom to top; an imported model follows its own texture layout.
hologram.fxHint: Scanlines and edge glow are code effects on this attachment in game; each takes one code-effect slot.
holoSets.title: Hologram sets
holoSets.menuHint: Several matching holograms at once, placed on the gun’s parts
holoSets.noPart: Open an item with a model first.
character.title: Character model
character.titleInfo: Replace your character with an imported humanoid model. Work down the steps on the left: import, bones, hair and skirt, materials, then export.
character.emptyText: Drop a .glb or .vrm file on the window, or pick one below. The model needs a humanoid skeleton and skinning.
character.dropHint: No model yet. You can also drop a .glb or .vrm on the window.
character.modelInfo: Skinned .glb and .vrm models with a humanoid skeleton work (Mixamo, VRoid, Blender exports). Bones, spring bones and colliders a VRM sets are filled in for you.
character.notSkinned: This model has no skinning, so it cannot be a character. Rig it in Blender and export the .glb again.
character.sameBoneNames: Some bones share a name. Give every bone its own name and export again.
character.needModel: Import a model in step 1 first.
character.bonesInfo: In game the character copies the original moves, so each joint needs its bone. Names were matched automatically; click a joint to pick its bone by hand. Green is matched, red needs a fix.
character.rematchInfo: Drop your picks and match by name again.
character.bonesReady: Every bone is matched and the rest pose checks out.
character.missingJoint: No bone for {{v0}}: click to pick one
character.issue.samePoint: {{v0}} and {{v1}} sit on one point: a bone is probably wrong
character.issue.standing: {{v0}} is {{v1}}° off: the bone is wrong or the model is not upright
character.issue.sides: {{v0}} is on the right side: left and right are swapped
character.backwards: The model faces backwards; the game turns it round.
character.fingersStillInfo: Not all 15 finger joints of this hand are matched, so its fingers keep the model's own pose in game.
character.pickJointInfo: Click a joint on the figure or a finger square, then choose its bone here.
character.pickJointHint: Click a joint above to change its bone.
character.armsInfo: The arms and hands you see in first person.
character.armsText: The game makes the first-person arms from this model itself: it keeps what is skinned to the upper arms and below (forearms, hands, fingers, sleeves) and puts each joint on the game's own arm, so the hands hold every weapon where the original hands do. You do not make a second model.
character.armsHideInfo: Switch on the materials that should not show in first person, such as a sleeve that would cover the sights. The arms view leaves them out as the game does.
character.armsEmpty: Nothing is left on the arms: the model has nothing skinned to them, or every material on them is left out in first person. First person keeps the original arms.
character.armsNeedsBones: Match the bones in the {{step}} step first to see the first-person arms.
character.viewInfo: First-person arms shows only what the game keeps for the arms you see in first person, without the materials left out in step 3. The moves below play on it too.
character.springsInfo: Make hair, ponytail, skirt or ribbon bones swing. Pick a bone: if several bone strands hang below it (a skirt), each becomes a strand. Use the buttons above to preview.
character.addSpring: Pick a bone to make it swing
character.springTooShort: No bones hang below this one, so nothing can swing. Pick one higher up.
character.collidersInfo: Hair and skirts are pushed off these blue capsules instead of passing through the body. The slider sets each capsule's size.
character.motionGameInfo: The game's own player animations. In the game your character follows the player's body the same way.
character.motionTryInfo: Extra Mixamo moves, to see how the model holds up in big movements.
character.motionNeedsBones: Match the bones in the {{step}} step first to play moves.
character.showBonesInfo: Draw the skeleton over the model.
character.shaderInfo: Which shader each material uses. Game lighting is the only one for now; it is lit like the game's own gear.
character.checkJoints: Every required joint has a bone
character.importedVrm: VRM imported: {{v0}} bones, {{v1}} spring sets and {{v2}} colliders filled in from the file.
character.reopenFailed: Could not open the last character skin: {{v0}}
character.heightInfo: In game the model is first scaled to the player's height (feet to head, measured on the bones), then by this. 1 is the player's height; 1.1 is a tenth taller.
character.creditInfo: The model’s licence asks for credit. Exports put it in the pack’s CREDITS.txt and the mod’s readme.
character.autoCollidersInfo: Drop the file’s colliders and use the seven capsules placed on the body instead, each switchable and sizable.
character.applyNotReady: Import a model and match its bones before trying it on in the game.
character.applyInfo: Installs this character skin into the test profile to try on. A running game shows it from the next level.
character.refused.not-glb: This is not a .glb or .vrm file.
character.refused.mesh-too-large: The mesh is larger than the game can read in one piece (about 2 GB of mesh data).
character.refused.skin-bones: Too many bones or broken skin data; up to {{limit}} bones.
character.refused.skin-bone-name: Bone “{{name}}” has a repeated or unusable name. Give every bone its own name and export again.
character.refused.extension: The model uses an extension that cannot be read: “{{name}}”. Turn it off when exporting.
character.refused.compressed: The model is compressed ({{name}}). Export it without compression.
character.refused.external: The model points to outside files. Export it as a single .glb.
character.refused.empty: The model has no mesh to show.
character.refused.image-format: Texture “{{name}}” is not PNG or JPEG.
character.refused.image-too-large: Texture “{{name}}” is too large. Scale it down and export again.
character.refused.normal-missing: The model has no normals. Export it with normals.
character.refused.skin-influences: Some vertices follow more than 4 bones. Limit them to 4 per vertex when exporting.
character.joint.head: Head
works.picturesGone: This work uses pictures that are no longer there: {{v0}}. They were deleted or moved.
works.picturesUnreadable: This work has pictures the editor cannot read: {{v0}}. They are not a picture format it reads (such as the game's compressed DDS), or the files are damaged.
works.picturesFix: The card and the preview show the game's own pictures in their place. Open the work and choose a PNG or JPG for those spots; if you no longer want the work, you can simply delete it.
works.changedInfo: You changed this work after it went into the profile; the game still has the old one. Apply to replace it.
works.applyInfo: Pack it, put it in the profile and make it this gear's skin in game. A running game shows it in seconds.
works.installedOnly: “{{v0}}” is in “{{v1}}”; the game still wears the one before, which you can change on the game's skin page
works.noCharacterCopy: Characters cannot be copied yet; import the same model again instead.
works.noWeaponWorks: No weapon skins yet. Click + New and pick a gear to start.
works.adoptAllInfo: Makes every editable pack here one of your works; the packs stay in the profile.
works.lostEditor: Packs keep no editing notes: set the livery and texture sizes again.
works.lost.compressed: Textures come back from the game's compressed copy, slightly softer.
works.lost.source: Characters come back with the model as the pack converted it; the bone match, springs, colliders, first-person hiding and height can still be changed. The model file it was made from is not in the pack, so the model itself cannot be imported again.
works.lost.frames: Animated layers come back as their baked frames; the source video, GIF or text is not in the pack. Position and size stay.
works.lost.layers: Some animated layers have no frames in the pack and were left out.
works.lost.meshes: Attachments keep only their game mesh; the source GLB is not in the pack.
works.lost.screens: A screen's font is not in the pack; it shows in the default font.
works.lost.missing: Some files are missing from the pack; they are marked once the work opens.
works.noCharacterWorks: No characters yet. Click + New to import a .vrm or .glb.
works.addPacksInfo: Install .forgeskin packs someone gave you into this profile, several at once. They do not replace the skins in use.
works.othersCount: {{v0}} more by others in this profile
works.othersInfo: These skins came from others, were put into the profile by hand or come from other skin mods; the editor has no project for them. You can Apply them, or Move to my works to edit them. A skin mod's belong to the mod manager and cannot be taken out here.
works.pickGear: Pick a gear for the new skin
works.removed: "{{v0}}" is out of "{{v1}}"; the pack is in the Recycle Bin
start.title: Make something
start.weaponInfo: Pick a gear; change textures, paint it, add attachments
start.characterInfo: Import a .vrm or .glb to replace the player character
settings.uninstallBody: Uninstall the skin plugin from "{{v0}}"? Gear and characters in game go back to the original look. Installed packs stay in the profile and come back when the plugin is installed again.
app.hotLive: Game running: an apply shows in a few seconds
app.hotIdle: Game not running: shows at the next launch
works.pluginUpdate: Skin plugin {{v0}}; the editor ships {{v1}}, update due
skinInspector.author: Author
skinInspector.tilesInfo: Each tile counts what the skin has of that kind. Click one to open the first part that has it, or to add one when there is none.
skinInspector.missingInfo: On: parts and texture channels the skin does not replace stay as the game draws them. Off: applying first lists what is still missing.
schemes.title: Colour schemes
schemes.info: Ready-made sets of values for the player colours. The game's colour page shows them as cards players switch with one click. Original is every player colour's default. Click a card to see it here; colour changes then go into that set.
schemes.needColors: Make at least one colour player-adjustable with the person button next to it before saving schemes.
schemes.addInfo: Save the colours shown now as a new scheme
playerColors.noTint: A gun's materials draw with the game's own shader, which has no tint, so a player's change would not show. Use a glow colour or an attachment colour instead.
character.checkInfo: What export needs. With every line ticked, export the mod from Export in the top bar.
